Hi Sam — good questions. High level summary below, attaching a compact matrix (backup_retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) that maps tiers to timelines.

- Short answer on recoverability: deleted data becomes non-addressable in the active store immediately, but may remain in immutable backup snapshots for a retention window. We perform logical delete in the primary dataset at request time; snapshots/tombstones follow the retention policy below.
- Retention tiers in that matrix: Hot snapshots (daily) = 7 days; Warm (weekly) = 30 days; Cold (monthly) = 90 days.
- Deletion propagation: our sweep job marks the deleted objects and they are excluded from restores starting immediately. Physical eradication (bytes-on-disk) depends on the tier lifecycle and reclaim processes — see matrix.
- Legal holds: when a hold is applied to an account or tag, that account is flagged in the legal-hold index and excluded from automated sweep jobs. Holds can be scoped to account, project, or dataset ID.

I'll pull in engineering to confirm exact background sweeps and any cross-region replication caveats. Attached: backup_retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (summary).

Hi Sam / Hannah — quick technical write-up below to confirm.

1) Immutability and tiers:
- Hot (daily snapshots): snapshots are incrementally immutable for 48 hours (write-protected), then become subject to mark-and-sweep.
- Warm (weekly consolidated snapshots): stored as versioned snapshots for 30 days; logical tombstone markers are applied immediately on delete and excluded from restores.
- Cold (monthly archival): retained 90 days before lifecycle expires and object deletion is scheduled.

2) Physical deletion timeline (post logical-delete):
- Hot: excluded from restores immediately; reclaimed by garbage collector between 7-14 days depending on GC window and retention configs.
- Warm: reclaimed at the 30-day lifecycle checkpoint; background reclaim may take up to an additional 14 days for compaction/manifest updates.
- Cold: scheduled for deletion ~90 days after snapshot creation; final byte-level erasure from object storage depends on provider lifecycle and can take an additional 30 days.

3) Legal hold behavior:
- Applying a legal hold sets a hard flag in the metadata index for the account/dataset. All automated sweep jobs check the index and skip flagged items; lifecycle transitions are paused for held items.
- Holds are propagated to all replica regions within the next replication cycle (usually < 4 hours), but physical deletion windows for cold tiers may still be longer due to provider-level lifecycle delays.

4) Replication & KMS caveats:
- Cross-region replicas are eventually consistent for lifecycle metadata; we replicate the legal-hold flag as a priority, but the actual immutable snapshot copies may still exist in the remote region until the remote sweep runs. Expect up to 48 hours for full cross-region alignment under heavy load.
- If customer-managed KMS is used, key access revocation is an additional lever: revoking keys will make cold snapshot data unrecoverable even if bytes persist, but note that this is an irreversible action and requires agreement from the customer.
